facts.text: I have a cough bringing up phlegm.
The breathlessness and cough came on suddenly 2 days ago, together with the fever, chills, aches and chest pain.
I have chest pain that gets worse when I breathe in.
I have benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.
Since childhood I've been admitted to hospital many times for pneumonia that keeps coming back.
Some of those infections were with Nocardia and Moraxella.
In the past five years I also had one episode of Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare infection.
I don't know of any contact with people who had tuberculosis.

findings.name: complete blood count
findings.result: White-cell count 13,500/µl with immature granulocytosis; no eosinophilia.

findings.name: chest radiograph
findings.result: Hyperexpansion of the lungs, bronchiectasis in the right suprahilar region and left lung base, and a right-sided aortic arch.

findings.name: noncontrast CT of the chest (inspiratory and expiratory)
findings.result: Inspiratory images: hyperinflation of both lungs and multiple ballooning cystic bronchiectasis distal to the third-generation bronchi bilaterally; coronal minimal-intensity-projection images confirm cystic bronchiectasis in the fourth- to sixth-order bronchi in the right upper and left lower lobes, with calcified hilar lymph nodes and a right-sided aortic arch. End-expiratory images: collapse of these bronchiectatic airways, also on expiratory coronal images. Oblique volume-rendered reconstruction: cystic bronchiectasis in the left lower lobe.

findings.name: pulmonary function tests
findings.result: Obstructive pattern with progression to fixed airway obstruction; no reversibility after bronchodilator administration.

findings.name: quantitative immunoglobulins
findings.result: IgG, IgA, IgM and IgE within normal limits.

findings.name: autoimmune serology
findings.result: Antinuclear antibody negative; rheumatoid factor negative.

gold.reasoning: 1. Cystic fibrosis was excluded by a normal sweat chloride test — “The sweat chloride test was negative.” 2. Hypogammaglobulinemia and other immunodeficiencies were excluded by normal quantitative immunoglobulin levels — “quantification of serum IgG, IgA, IgE and IgM levels, which were normal.” 3. Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis was excluded by normal Aspergillus‐specific immunoglobulins — “Anti Aspergillus immunoglobulins were within the normal range.” 4. Tuberculosis and nontuberculous mycobacterial infection were excluded by negative sputum acid-fast bacilli smear and culture and absence of risk factors — “the sputum sample for acid-fast bacilli was negative.” 5. Fungal pulmonary infection was excluded by negative sputum fungal cultures — “sputum sample sent for fungal cultures did not report any growth.” 6. Rheumatic causes of bronchiectasis were excluded by negative serologies — “Anti-nuclear antibody and serum rheumatoid factors were negative.”
